Exact_Manuscript_Wording: In simulations, accuracy collapses with noise dimensions and subsample stability collapses alongside it, so evidence for stability--accuracy discordance rests on the real cohorts.
Supporting_Theory: Beyer et al. (1999) distance concentration theorem under isotropic Gaussian noise.
Safe_Wording: In isotropic simulations, accuracy and stability collapse together as noise dimensions grow, confirming that synthetic isotropic noise alone does not produce discordance.

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: Three of twelve methods (FCAG, FCM, FastMVC) show non-degenerate discordance on three cohorts each. Across these nine cells, mean stability is 0.684 and mean accuracy is -0.003 (permuted null ~ 0.01).
Supporting_Theory: Resampling fixed finite-sample realizations with D >> N repeatedly draws the same empirical spurious covariance.
Safe_Wording: Three of twelve methods (FCAG, FCM, FastMVC) show non-degenerate discordance on three cohorts each, averaging 0.684 stability and -0.003 accuracy against permuted nulls of ~0.01.

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: A cohort-clustered bootstrap confirms a positive gap of +0.485 (95% CI [+0.379, +0.662]; unconstrained +0.464), showing that reproducibility does not imply correctness.
Supporting_Theory: Dataset-clustered bootstrap (B=10,000) preserving intra-cohort sample correlation.
Safe_Wording: A cohort-clustered bootstrap confirms a positive stability-accuracy gap of +0.485 (95% CI [+0.379, +0.662]; unconstrained +0.464).

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: Bipartite compression reduces consensus-graph memory by 99.6% at N = 10^4.
Supporting_Theory: Dense matrix requires N(N-1)/2 floats (762.9 MB at N=10,000); bipartite requires N x L floats (3.05 MB at L=40).
Safe_Wording: Bipartite graph compression reduces auxiliary consensus-graph storage by 99.6% at N = 10^4 (3.05 MB vs. 762.9 MB), with a 97.4% reduction in total process heap memory (68.8 MB vs. 2,670.6 MB).

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: Proposition 1: For a standard unimodal Gaussian distractor distribution, gamma = 0 and kappa = 0, yielding E[b_d] ~ 1/3 ~ 0.333. For continuous uniform, b_d = 5/9 ~ 0.556. Mixture b_d > 5/9 iff Delta/sigma_0 > 1.854.
Supporting_Theory: Exact Pearson kurtosis and Sarle BC moment derivation.
Safe_Wording: Proposition 1 (Conditional Multimodality Separation Bound for Symmetric Densities): For symmetric unimodal distributions, b <= 5/9, with uniform reaching 5/9. For balanced two-component symmetric Gaussian mixtures, b > 5/9 iff Delta/sigma_0 > 1.854.

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: Proposition 2: Exact determinacy identity computes sample determinacy in O(M^2 N + M^2 K^2) time and O(N + K^2) working memory without materializing S.
Supporting_Theory: Algebraic contingency matrix reformulation of quadratic co-association sum.
Safe_Wording: Proposition 2 (Exact Determinacy Identity): The contingency formulation computes quadratic determinacy in O(M^2 N + M^2 K^2) time and O(N + K^2) working memory without materializing S.

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: Theorem 1: Computational complexity of GAC pipeline is T_GAC = O(ND + D log D + M^2 N + M^2 K^2 + M I_km N |F_sub| K + M N L + N L^2 + L^3 + N L K + I_km N K^2), scaling linearly O(N) for fixed ensemble parameters.
Supporting_Theory: Sum of step complexities in Algorithm 1 under fixed L, M, K.
Safe_Wording: Theorem 1 (Complexity): Overall time complexity scales linearly as O(N) for fixed ensemble parameters, with auxiliary working graph memory bounded by O(NL + L^2).

Exact_Manuscript_Wording: Centroid assignment in active subspace (Eq. 9-10) avoids recomputing consensus graph upon arrival of new observations in O(K |F_active|) time.
Supporting_Theory: Euclidean nearest centroid classifier in R^{|F_active|}.
Safe_Wording: Active subspace centroid projection maps new observations in O(K |F_active|) time without graph recomputation, strictly under the assumption of convex, hyper-ellipsoidal cluster geometry (failing on non-convex manifolds).
